title_en: Xu Jun — embezzlement and bribery case
keywords_en: Criminal; Embezzlement; Acceptance of Bribes; Second Instance; High People's Court; Beijing; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery; Whether Depositing Public Funds in Personal Accounts Constitutes Embezzlement; Affirmance of Original Judgment; Embezzlement of Public Funds; Acceptance of Bribes; Abuse of Official Position
full_text_en:
Xu Jun — embezzlement and acceptance of bribes

Defendant: Xu Jun, male, 61 years old, former Director of the Transport Bureau of the Ministry of Railways. Arrested on October 25, 1989.

The case of defendant Xu Jun for embezzlement and acceptance of bribes was initiated by the Branch Procuratorate of Beijing Municipal People's Procuratorate, which filed a public prosecution with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court. The Beijing Intermediate People's Court, after public trial, found the following facts:

In February 1987, China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Sinopec), after consultations with the Beijing Railway Bureau and other entities, arranged for heavy oil to be transferred from Jinxi Refinery to Beijing, with the railway department charging 30% above the original transport rate. This fee was borne by Sinopec. On May 23, Sinopec allocated more than RMB 230,000 to the Beijing Railway Bureau under the name of "fee for tapping potential and improving efficiency." After learning of this matter, defendant Xu Jun decided that the Beijing Railway Bureau should transfer RMB 50,000 of this amount to the account of the Institute of Transport Economics, Academy of Railway Sciences (hereinafter referred to as the Institute of Transport Economics). In January 1988, the Yangquan Municipal People's Government of Shanxi Province planned to use three self-owned trains of the Yangquan Coal Transportation Branch to transport coal to Shandong. After consultations with the Transport Bureau of the Ministry of Railways, the Beijing Railway Bureau, and other entities, it was decided that for each ton of coal transported, the Yangquan Coal Transportation Branch would pay a service fee of RMB 2 to the railway department, of which 10% would go to the Transport Bureau of the Ministry of Railways. Pursuant to Xu Jun's instruction, by July 1988, Yangquan had remitted service fees totaling RMB 60,649.40 to the Transport Bureau of the Ministry of Railways into the account of the Institute of Transport Economics. Subsequently, Xu Jun directed the head of the Institute to withdraw cash from these two sums on six occasions, totaling RMB 95,149.40. From this cash, Xu Jun used RMB 1,005 for public purposes of the Transport Bureau of the Ministry of Railways, paid RMB 1,800 as a "handling fee" to the head of the Institute of Transport Economics, and deposited the remaining RMB 92,344.40 in banks under his own name and the names of his relatives, appropriating it for himself.

In April 1987, during the Transport Bureau of the Ministry of Railways' involvement in transporting large generator components for Shihuang Power Plant in Shandong Province, it was entitled to a supervision and transport fee of RMB 30,000. Defendant Xu Jun instructed others to remit this amount to the Qiqihar Audio-Visual Factory, where it was fully withdrawn as cash through the factory's head. Xu Jun distributed RMB 25,000 of this amount as bonuses within the Transport Bureau of the Ministry of Railways, gave RMB 3,000 as a "handling fee" to the Qiqihar Audio-Visual Factory, and retained the remaining RMB 2,000 for himself.

In 1988, the Transport Bureau of the Ministry of Railways decided to publish four books of the "Safety Manual" on freight, passenger transport, loading and unloading, and train operations, which were organized and compiled by the Bureau and reviewed by Xu Jun, through the Qiqihar Audio-Visual Factory under China Railway Publishing House. The Qiqihar Audio-Visual Factory, following notice from the publishing house, paid manuscript fees and review fees respectively to the authors and reviewer Xu Jun, and also gave the Transport Bureau cash and remittances totaling RMB 9,918 under the name of "manuscript fees." After receiving this amount, Xu Jun kept RMB 1,718 for public use and deposited the remaining RMB 8,200 in a bank under his own name, appropriating it for himself.

Between April 1988 and February 1989, after resolving transport issues such as providing off-plan train usage for the Zhengzhou Railway Bureau Travel Comprehensive Service Company, Changchun Railway Station, and the Shanghai Railway Bureau Foreign Service Company, defendant Xu Jun successively accepted bribes totaling RMB 25,500 and one Bingxiong brand freezer worth RMB 2,354 from the aforesaid entities.

Between April 1988 and January 1989, defendant Xu Jun, together with Hu Junle and Ma Mingshan (both separately prosecuted), after resolving railway freight transport issues for the Guangdong Shunde Xianfo Sanlian Industrial Company, accepted bribes from the company on three occasions totaling RMB 15,000, of which Xu Jun received RMB 6,200.

In total, the above defendant Xu Jun embezzled public funds amounting to RMB 102,000, accepted bribes of RMB 31,700 and one freezer. All proceeds of Xu Jun's embezzlement and bribery have been recovered.

The above facts are confirmed by material evidence, documentary evidence, witness testimony, and the defendant Xu Jun's confession.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court held that: Defendant Xu Jun, as a state functionary, took advantage of his position to embezzle public funds, and his conduct constituted the crime of embezzlement under Article 155, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China; Xu Jun took advantage of his position to accept bribes, and his conduct constituted the crime of accepting bribes under Article 185, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. The amount of public funds Xu Jun embezzled was exceptionally large and the circumstances were particularly serious; in accordance with Paragraph 2, Item (1) of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Concerning the Punishment of Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery, he should be severely punished; based on the facts and circumstances of Xu Jun's crime of embezzlement, in accordance with Article 53, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, he shall be deprived of political rights for life. The amount of bribes Xu Jun accepted was large and the circumstances were serious; in accordance with Article 5, Paragraph 1 and Paragraph 2, Item (2) of the Supplementary Provisions, he should be punished; Xu Jun's criminal conduct of accepting bribes severely undermined social order, and in accordance with Article 52 of the Criminal Law, deprivation of political rights may be imposed as a supplementary punishment. After being subjected to compulsory measures, Xu Jun confessed to criminal facts not yet known to the procuratorial authorities and actively returned the illicit gains. In accordance with Paragraph 2, Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate's Notice Concerning the Requirement that Criminals of Embezzlement, Bribery, and Speculation Must Surrender and Confess Within a Specified Period, he may be given a comparatively lenient punishment. Xu Jun committed multiple crimes, and in accordance with Article 64 of the Criminal Law, he shall be punished for multiple crimes. The illicit money and goods obtained by Xu Jun through embezzlement and bribery shall be recovered in accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law and Article 12 of the Supplementary Provisions. In accordance with Paragraph 2, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Supplementary Provisions, Xu Jun shall also be sentenced to confiscation of property. Accordingly, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 23, 1990:

1. Defendant Xu Jun is convicted of embezzlement and sentenced to death, with a two-year suspension of execution, and deprivation of political rights for life; convicted of accepting bribes and sentenced to ten years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for two years; the combined sentence is death, with a two-year suspension of execution, and deprivation of political rights for life.

2. The recovered illicit funds of RMB 133,700 and one freezer, being illicit goods, shall be recovered.

3. A portion of defendant Xu Jun's personal property is confiscated.

After the first instance judgment, defendant Xu Jun appealed to the Beijing High People's Court, arguing that "his conduct was depositing public funds in a personal account and did not constitute the crime of embezzlement."

The Beijing High People's Court held at trial that: Appellant Xu Jun, as a state functionary, took advantage of his position to embezzle public funds and accept bribes, and his conduct constituted the crimes of embezzlement and acceptance of bribes. Moreover, the circumstances of his crime of embezzlement were particularly serious and should be severely punished according to law. When Xu Jun withdrew public funds temporarily deposited in the account of the Institute of Transport Economics, he instructed the handler "not to tell anyone about this." Later, in the second half of 1989, when Xu Jun learned of a financial inspection, he instructed others to delete the record of the money remitted into the Institute of Transport Economics' account. When that goal was not achieved, Xu Jun further instructed others to cover up the truth of the withdrawal of public funds by signing a false contract. After Xu Jun no longer held the position of Director of the Transport Bureau, and until he was subjected to compulsory measures in this case, he never informed the succeeding Transport Bureau leader about the existence of this sum of money. Thus, Xu Jun's appeal argument that his conduct was "depositing public funds in a personal account" and did not constitute the crime of embezzlement cannot be sustained. The facts found in the original judgment are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, the legal characterization is correct, the sentence is appropriate, and the trial procedures are lawful. Accordingly, the Beijing High People's Court, in accordance with Article 136, Item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled on January 7, 1991: to reject appellant Xu Jun's appeal and affirm the original judgment.

In accordance with Article 146 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Beijing High People's Court approved the criminal judgment of the Beijing Intermediate People's Court sentencing defendant Xu Jun to death, with a two-year suspension of execution, and deprivation of political rights for life for the crime of embezzlement; to ten years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for two years for the crime of accepting bribes; and the combined sentence of death, with a two-year suspension of execution.
